adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 section 9 whole. It has no paragraph on rulings, so the proposal's anchor 'after the paragraph on rulings' names text that is not there; the paragraph is simply new, at the end of section 9. v6 nowhere says who may write row text or how text ordered by a ruling is tested, so the substance is not already present. It contradicts nothing: it is section 7's working rule (a mandated mechanical re-check of the finished artefact before return, with the count reported) applied to one more author, and section 12's preference for a tool over a caution. It would have caught each case I checked one round earlier: in every one the suite or sweep that later raised the flag already existed when the span was ordered, and the fix-up author who saw the flag was forbidden to depart from the verbatim order. It is not fitted to one accident: four separate rulings (E1, E2 through the W4-003 order, E4, E9) ordered a span that raised a flag, on three different members (web_quotes, register, the reference-notation pattern) and the five-word rule. Blast radius campaign_wide is honest only for books that use a ruling role issuing exact spans; I say so in the text. Cost is understated in one respect: the ruling role must be given the suite and what it imports, which E1 unresolved_uncertainty[1] and [2] record it was not. Two corrections to the wording. First, the proposer's own objection is sound: a role that both judges and measures can reword to silence a true flag. I add that the dry run may be run for the ruling role by a tool, and that a span reworded because of a flag keeps the first wording and the flag in the ruling record. Second, the control was not run in Daniel, so the text says what was measured (the cost of its absence) and that the control itself is untried, as section 13 asks.
adjudications.adopted_text: **Text ordered by a ruling is row text, and is tested as row text before the ruling is issued (new in v7, M8, Daniel).** When a ruling role orders an exact replacement span, that role is writing the row. Before the ruling is issued, each ordered span is applied to a scratch copy of the current rows and the whole validator suite and every corpus-wide sweep are run on that copy. The ruling records, per span, which flags were gained and which were lost, by flag key. A span that gains a flag is reworded before issue, or the ruling disposes that flag by its key and gives the reason; where a span was reworded because of a flag, the ruling keeps the first wording and the flag beside the one it issues, so a later reader can see that a flag was weighed and not merely avoided. The tool that applies ordered spans refuses a span with no recorded dry run. The dry run may be run for the ruling role by a tool; the ruling role must in either case be given the suite and everything the suite imports as pinned inputs. Measured in Daniel: four rulings ordered a span that raised a flag the suite already knew how to raise, on three suite members and on the rule against unquoted runs of witness words; the fix-up author who saw the flag was bound to the order's exact words and could not cure it; one whole repair round existed to undo one ordered span, and one author execution was run twice. Daniel did not run this control. It measured the cost of lacking it, so the control is handed forward as untried: the first book to run it records how many spans it changed before issue.
adjudications.adopted_text_differs_from_proposal: Kept: the scratch-copy dry run, the per-span flag delta, reword or dispose by key, refusal by the apply tool. Added: the first wording and its flag are kept when a span is reworded; the dry run may be run by a tool for the ruling role; the suite and its imports are pinned to that role; the measured basis from Daniel; the statement that the control is untried. Dropped: nothing. The anchor is corrected from 'after the paragraph on rulings' to 'end of section 9'.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 section 5, section 8, section 16 item 10 and section 18. Part of the proposal is already there. Section 5 says to enumerate and settle conventions, but its trigger is 'before a review wave' and its instrument is the reviewers' brief; it does not reach the writers and names no check. Section 8 already says to make the dual-reference rule 'a hard gate with a mechanical check' as a Phase-0 artefact, so the proposal's sentence on verse-reference notation repeats section 8; I keep it only as a cross-reference. Section 16 item 10 and section 18 already say to enforce the tier in a tool; neither says when. What is new, and what Daniel's evidence shows, is the timing and the test of 'settled': the strategy stated the tier rule in prose before the writers ran (book_strategy_Dan.md line 6), no suite member checked it, and the third ruling then found 49 of 75 rows with a prose field carrying no tier word and had to write the allowed form as a regex after the fact. A rule that was in force and did not hold is evidence for the tool, not for more prose. It contradicts section 12 if read without limit: 'a convention counts as settled only when a hard suite member enforces it' would turn every convention into a tool, and some cannot be checked by form (E4 unresolved_uncertainty[6]: no script proves a tier word true). I narrow it to conventions checkable by form and require the text to say what the check does not prove. One clause contradicts a standing Daniel ruling: 'never left standing in two forms' is the opposite of E7 P9-CARRIED-ANNOTATION and E8 OLD-FORM-UNCHANGED, which left old-form annotations in unchanged sentences and routed them to the end review. I do not overrule that ruling for Daniel; for later books I adopt the sweep as the default and require a recorded list of rows where it is not done, because two forms of one annotation in a closed book is what section 18 calls a record that keeps the shape of its neighbours while meaning something else. Also added from E3 unresolved_uncertainty[1]: two conventions (name the file beside the tier word; no file stems in prose) contradicted each other and met for the first time in the third ruling. Stated blast radius campaign_wide is honest for the tier layer, which every book carries. The cost is honest as far as I can test it: I did not open the E3 gate conditions' regex itself.
adjudications.adopted_text:
**A convention is settled when it is written as a pattern and a check for it is installed before the WRITERS run, not only before the reviewers (new in v7, M8, Daniel).** This section's rule was in force for Daniel and did not hold for the tier layer: the book's strategy stated the tier rule in prose before any row was written, no validator member checked it, and the third ruling found 49 of 75 rows with at least one prose field carrying no tier word. A whole repair round followed, and the allowed annotation form was first written down as a pattern in that ruling, after the rows existed. So, for every convention that can be checked by its form:

1. Before the writer brief is built, the strategy gives the convention as the pattern the tool uses, and a validator member that fails on a breach is installed and shown to fail (section 12).
2. For the tier layer (section 18) the strategy fixes, before any row is written: which fields must carry a tier word; the one allowed annotation form; the tier of a negative claim, of a language-zone claim and of a mark-layer claim; and that a missing tier word in a required field is a defect and not a note. Daniel's reviewers and its ruling role each had to ask these questions of the finished rows.
3. The same holds for placeholder strings, and for reference notation in a numbering zone (section 8 already requires that check in Phase 0; Daniel still rewrote 16 references after its writers ran).
4. Check the conventions against each other before the writers run. In Daniel one rule asked for the file name beside the tier word and another barred file names in row prose; they met for the first time in the third ruling.
5. A convention introduced or changed by ruling after the writers have run is applied to every row in one sweep. Where it is not, the close record lists by row id every row left in the earlier form. Daniel closed with one annotation standing in two forms, by a ruling that routed the older form to the end review; a later reader cannot tell the two forms apart without that list.

**What the check does not prove.** A form check proves that a tier word stands where one is required. It does not prove that the word is the true tier; Daniel's ruling role recorded that no script it had proved that. The truth of a tier stays a reviewer's question, and the brief says so, so that a passing check is not read as a verified tier and a writer is not taught to add a word in order to pass.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 section 7 whole. It is about quotation: load both witnesses, never quote from memory, re-check the finished artefact. It has no sentence on runs of witness words that stand unquoted, so the proposal's 'the rule against unquoted runs' names a rule the method record does not yet state; the adopted text must introduce it. The substance (one predicate, given to lanes) is not present anywhere in v6; section 5 says conventions are settled in the brief but the M8 examples it lists do not include this one. It contradicts nothing. It would have caught the cost earlier: three rulings each settled one piece (E1 on what counts as a word of the other member, E6 on fields and comparison set and hyphens, E9 on punctuation), and ten primary packets by my keyword scan spent an uncertainty entry on the question. It is not fitted to one accident. One sentence of the proposal is wrong on Daniel's own evidence: 'files it as a tool finding against the predicate, not as a row finding'. E9 PEER-W6-006 ruled a run found by reading 'true on the bytes' and ordered a span; had it been filed only against the tool the row would have kept the defect. I change this to both. The proposer's own objection (lanes given the predicate stop looking where the tool is blind) is answered in the text and not waved away: the predicate tells a reader where the tool looks, and the brief says the reader's duty is the rule, not the predicate. The Greek objection is met by stating the predicate per witness in each book's strategy; Daniel tested Hebrew, Aramaic and an English witness only. Blast radius campaign_wide is honest: every book has the rule. Cost is honest; the fixture set is section 12's must-fail rule.
adjudications.adopted_text:
**The rule against unquoted runs of witness words has one predicate, and lanes are given it (new in v7, M8, Daniel).** Words of a witness that stand in a row are quoted and cited. A run of consecutive witness words standing unquoted is a defect, and a tool checks for it. The strategy states the predicate that tool uses, per witness, before the writers run (section 5): the length of a run; how words are tokenised (case, punctuation, hyphen, apostrophe); which row fields are scanned, tag and gloss text included; and which witness verses a field is compared with (the row's own span and the verses the field cites, or the whole book). The statement is generated from the tool's own constants, and the tool carries a must-fail fixture for each clause (section 12). Measured in Daniel: three separate rulings each settled one clause after the rows existed, and ten of eleven primary review packets searched carry an uncertainty entry on how the tool counts a run.

**The predicate tells a reader where the tool looks; it does not tell the reader to look only there.** A reviewer who finds, by reading, a run the tool did not report files it twice: as a row finding, ruled on the witness bytes, and as a tool finding against the predicate, which is corrected before the next round. In Daniel a peer reader found five consecutive witness words in an evidence entry after the suite had passed the row, and the ruling held the finding true on the bytes; filed against the tool alone, the row would have kept the defect. Daniel tested this with a Hebrew and Aramaic witness and an English one. The predicate for a Greek witness is untried and is stated in the strategy of the first book that has one.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 sections 6, 12, 13 and 14. Section 12 already says to prefer a generator fix and to give a validator a negative control; it speaks of validators, not of a generated pattern layer that writers read as data, so the control per pattern is new. Section 14 already says a figure read is not a figure measured and that counts are to be carried by tool; a position stated by hand in a row is the same failure in a new place, and v6 does not name it. Section 13 lists as open (question 6) how device-class labels should be fixed; this proposal answers one part of it from a book that tested it. Nothing in v6 is contradicted. It would have caught the cost earlier: the inventory already labelled the 6:11 hit a homograph and held strict and loose classes apart, and the rows still used them as one, because (on the proposal's account, which I could not test from the brief files) the label did not reach the writer; and every false position I read (E6 ROW-W6-010, E9 PEER-W4-007, E9 PEER-W6-015, E12 RR9-TB-W4-004) is checkable by tokenising one witness line. The last of these was the whole content of a tenth repair round. It is not fitted to one accident: four rulings, three review stages. Three corrections. (a) The closed list 'formula, loose form, token artefact, homograph' is Daniel's list; another book's layer will have other classes, so the method fixes that the list is closed by the strategy and names Daniel's four as the example. (b) The convention for word positions is stated as the proposal has it, but as the convention of the pinned extract, with the sentence peer_g05 supplies: a reader of a printed edition counts differently, so a row that states a position names the convention. (c) The extent of a pattern's match is carried into the row from the layer by tool, not restated; this is what RR9-TB-W4-004 shows and the proposal leaves implicit. Blast radius: campaign_wide overstates; the layer rule reaches only books whose strategy builds a pattern layer, and the position check reaches any book whose rows state positions. I say so. The proposer's objection that a checker invites position sentences is fair and is answered by not requiring them. The control per pattern was not run in Daniel and is handed forward as untried. The proposal's target of two sections is reduced to one paragraph in section 12 with the word-count convention inside it; section 6 is about parent selection and is the wrong home.
adjudications.adopted_text:
**A pattern layer is released to writers with its controls, its class labels and its extents, and a stated position is checked by the suite (new in v7, M8, Daniel).** Where a book's strategy builds a pattern layer (an inventory of devices or formulae found by pattern over a witness), the layer is a generated artefact that writers will read as fact, and it meets the standard of this section before the writer wave:

1. For every pattern, one verse where it must hit and one where it must not, each checked by hand against the witness, recorded in the layer.
2. For every hit, a class label from a list the strategy closes before the writers run. Daniel's list was: formula, loose form, token artefact, homograph. Writers and reviewers receive the labels, and a row may present a hit only as what its label says. Daniel's layer already called one hit a homograph and held a strict and a loose class apart; rows presented the homograph as the device and listed both classes under one label, and two rulings corrected them.
3. For every hit, its extent as word positions on the pinned witness line. A row that gives the extent of a hit takes it from the layer by tool and does not restate it. Daniel's tenth and last repair round was one device key given a range one word wider than the pattern's match.
4. Word positions use one convention, stated in the strategy: one-based, on the whitespace-separated tokens of the pinned witness line, a maqqef-joined group counted as the tokens that extract shows. A reader of a printed edition counts differently, so a row that states a position states it under this convention and the strategy says so once.
5. A row sentence of the form 'words N to M of K' is checked by a suite member against the witness line. The member exists to check positions a row already needs; no row is asked to state a position in order to be checked.

Measured in Daniel: four rulings at three stages corrected a row that misstated where a phrase stands or what the layer lists, and in each one read the boundary stood and only the description was wrong. Daniel pinned its layer before these defects were known and kept it pinned, so within a book the controls come before the writer wave or not at all. Daniel did not run the control of point 1; it is handed forward as untried, and the first book to run it records how many patterns it changed. This paragraph reaches only a book whose strategy builds such a layer; points 4 and 5 reach any book whose rows state word positions.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 sections 9, 13 and 19. Section 9 has nothing on repair rounds. Section 13 question 10 asks what a second reading owes a first and leaves it open; the last sentence of the proposal (record rounds and changed places at the close) gives that question its first measured answer and is the cheapest part. Section 19 sets two blind lanes as the floor and says a lane that reads the shipped rows of another is an audit, not a lane. Tested against these, the four parts fare differently. (1) Rounds and changed places recorded at the close: new, contradicts nothing, measured in Daniel by the boss lane (1, 2 and 28 places). Adopt. (2) Re-review lanes given the whole changed field and the finding the order answers: two lanes in two different rounds recorded the same limit in their own words. But rr8_OS says the finding texts were ones it 'may not open', so Daniel withheld them on purpose, presumably to keep the lane blind to the first reader's judgement. Section 19's blindness is between lanes judging the same thing; the defect a repair was ordered to cure is the lane's question, not a rival answer. I adopt it with the limit that the lane is given the statement of the defect and not the finder's grade or the other lane's verdict. (3) The author re-reads the whole of every field it changes: the proposer marks its benefit INFERRED and untested, and so do I; I could not show from the bytes that either late finding stood beside a changed sentence. It costs one author little, it is section 7's rule (re-check the finished artefact) applied to a repair, and I adopt it marked untried. (4) What opens a further round. The proposal's rule is: a sentence false to the witness always opens one; anything else on text the round did not change is routed. On Daniel's two late rounds this rule would have routed the ninth (a missing tier word) and kept the tenth (a false position). But E6 CLASS-TIER-WORD rules a missing tier word a defect, section 18 says the same, and the proposer's own strongest objection is that routing a known defect to an end review run on a fallback model leaves a known error in closed rows. The proposal's cost line says the rule is 'a judgement the owner or Fable must set'. I agree, and so I do not adopt the content of the rule. I adopt only that the strategy states it before the first round, by whoever has that authority, so that the ruling role does not decide it finding by finding at the end. Would the proposal have prevented Daniel's cost? Partly. The tenth round's fault was in a ruling's ordered text, which Dan-P01 and Dan-P04 address at the cause; this proposal addresses the lanes around it. Blast radius campaign_wide is honest. Cost is honest.
adjudications.adopted_text:
**Repair rounds: what the author re-reads, what the re-review lane is given, and what the close records (new in v7, M8, Daniel).** Daniel ran ten repair rounds. Its last two each had an author and two blind re-review lanes and changed one place each; the rows that closed differ from the rows three rounds earlier in 28 places in 21 rows (measured by the audit lane). Four rules follow, the first two measured and the last two untried.

1. The close records, per round, the number of places changed and what opened the round. This is the first measured answer to what a second reading costs and finds (section 13).
2. Before the first repair round the strategy states what opens a further round and what is carried to the end review instead. Who may set that rule is the owner's decision; the method record does not set its content. In Daniel it was unset, and the ruling role decided it finding by finding at the end: 'corrected now, not routed', twice. A rule set in advance may not route a sentence that is false to the witness, and a missing or false tier is a defect under section 18.
3. A fix-up author re-reads against the witness the whole of every field it changes, not only the changed span, and records that it did (section 7: re-check the finished artefact). Untried in Daniel.
4. A re-review lane is given the whole changed field and the statement of the defect the order answers, not the order text alone. It is not given the finder's grade or any other lane's verdict on the repair, so the lanes stay blind to each other (section 19). Two of Daniel's re-review lanes, in two rounds, recorded that they judged each change against the order's wording only and that a change can meet the order and still miss the finding. Untried in Daniel; the first book to run it records whether a lane so briefed finds what the order missed.

Added: what opened each round is recorded with the count; points 3 and 4 are marked untried; the measured figures.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 sections 9, 14, 16 item 10 and 18. Section 18 defines the tiers: MEASURED is what a script of this lane produced; EXTRACTED is what was read programmatically from a durable artefact at a named place; REPORTED is what another lane said. Section 14 says a figure read is not a figure measured. So the proposal's third sentence is already the rule in substance, and as worded it is slightly wrong against section 18: 'a value copied from a measurement file is REPORTED' collapses two claims. That the file says X is EXTRACTED when the file is pinned and the place named; that X is true is REPORTED, because another lane's run produced it. I adopt that sharper form, since the looser one would let a later reader think EXTRACTED from a measurement file is forbidden, or that REPORTED needs no file. What is new and what Daniel shows: (a) a gate condition must be testable from pinned bytes, and this is checked before launch. The audit lane returned on two of seventeen conditions for that cause alone, with 75 of 75 rows confirmed. (b) A lane that judges a tiered claim must hold the layer the tier names. Three rulings (E3, E4, E8) and two review lanes record ruling on, or passing over, MEASURED claims whose layer they did not have. Neither is in v6. Neither contradicts v6. Both would have prevented the cost; a brief-build check refuses the launch. Not fitted to one accident: five separate records at four stages. One narrowing: 'every lane that reviews that row' is wider than the evidence and than the budget allows (the proposer's own objection). A lane that does not judge a layer's claims need not hold the layer, provided it says so. I adopt: the layer is pinned to every lane whose brief asks it to judge that claim; any other lane records the claim as not tested by it, by tier and layer. That keeps the rule and bounds the context cost. The fourth evidence group (an unpinned library behind a pinned tool) supports a further sentence the proposal does not write: a pinned tool's imports are pinned with it. I add it; it is the same rule one step down, and Dan-P01 relies on it. Blast radius campaign_wide is honest. Cost honest; the check is in the brief builder.
adjudications.adopted_text:
In section 18, after 'Enforce it in a tool':

**A tiered claim is judged only by a lane that holds its layer, and a gate condition is testable before launch (new in v7, M8, Daniel).**

1. A lane writes MEASURED only for a value its own run produced from pinned bytes. A value taken from another lane's measurement file is two claims: that the file says it, which is EXTRACTED when the file is pinned and the place is named; and that it is true, which is REPORTED. The lane writes both and names the file. In Daniel a gate evaluation and a landing summary wrote MEASURED over values copied from a file that was not a pinned input, and the audit lane corrected the word.
2. A gate condition names, for its predicate and for each value it rests on, a pinned file and a place in it. The brief builder checks this before the lane launches; a condition whose predicate stands in no pinned byte is returned then. Daniel's audit lane confirmed 75 of 75 rows and still returned, because two of seventeen conditions could not be tested from the bytes it was given; a supplementary run cured it.
3. Every layer that a row's tier word names (in Daniel: the mark layer, the language-zone layer, the device inventory, the numbering crosswalk) is a pinned input of every lane whose brief asks it to judge a claim on that layer, the ruling role included. A lane without the layer does not pass over the claim in silence: it records, by row and layer, that the claim was not tested by it. In Daniel the ruling role three times recorded ruling without the layer behind the MEASURED language claims, and two review lanes could not test four records for want of the language-zone layer.
4. A pinned tool is pinned with everything it imports. In Daniel a pinned checker loaded an unpinned library.

In section 9, one line: a lane's brief lists the layers it holds, and its packet lists the tiered claims it could not test for want of one (section 18).

Narrowed: the layer is pinned to every lane asked to judge a claim on it, not to every lane that reviews the row; other lanes record the claim as untested. Added: the brief builder makes the check before launch (the proposal had this under cost); point 4 on a tool's imports, from the proposal's own fourth evidence group; the ruling role is named among the lanes. The citation of the supplement is corrected to its manifest path.

adjudications.method_record_check: Read v6 sections 9, 12 and 17. The reader of the method record is a chunker deciding how to cut and review a book; section 12 already tells that reader to prefer a generator fix to a caution and to keep a repair's scope narrow. Tested against v6: (1) Already there? Not as text; but the definition of a flag key is by Daniel's own rulings a property of one triage tool's report format (claim word and path, counted; a five-part tuple by the tenth ruling), and a method record that fixed it would be describing a tool, which the next generation's tool may not share. (2) Contradiction: the second half ('the brief that opens fields is built by tool from the orders, so that an order cannot name a field the brief leaves closed') pulls against section 12's scope discipline unless carefully built. In Daniel the narrow open-field list did what section 12 wants: thirteen blocked entries were recorded by the authors and closed by ruling, and nothing was changed outside an order. The first W4 entry I read shows the other side: a finding about tier words in a field was left uncured because the map did not open it. That is a real cost, and it is a fault in how the orders and the map were built, cured by building one from the other. (3) Would it have prevented Daniel's cost? Yes: a whole ruling execution accepted 38 entries and ordered nothing. (4) Fitted to one accident? It is fitted to one tool. (5) Blast radius and cost: the proposal gives none beyond the tool change, and its rating of itself is LOW_REWARD as method text. I agree with the proposer on every point of its own assessment. The fix is real and should be made; it is made in the triage tool and the fix-up brief builder, under section 12 as it stands, without new method text. Dan-P01's adopted paragraph speaks of flags 'by flag key' and so depends on the tool having one; that dependency is recorded in the cross-proposal notes and is a reason to make the tool fix, not a reason to put the key's definition in the method record.

Section 5 already says to enumerate the conventions a book will meet and settle them before the wave, and a typing rule for one-sided speech is such a convention; the strategy has a section for it. So the second half of the proposal asks for what section 5 and the strategy's own layout already provide, and the failure in Daniel, if it is one, is that the convention was not listed there. Dan-P02 as adopted strengthens that rule without naming this case. The first half (a new type, or a change to the closed list) is cross-generation by the proposal's own blast radius: it reaches every generation's rows and every closed book. Against that cost the evidence is one row of 75 whose type changed, and two lanes of one family noting a doubt about three other rows that no ruling changed in what I read. Section 13 says an untested rule is worse than an open question; a typing rule written here would be untested, since Daniel never applied one. Would it have prevented a cost?
